modv0.1.0

restPause every session with one command.

Each holds its next tool call with no model running, then resumes where it stopped, and nothing is lost.

At the prompt of a terminal session:

/plugin install rest --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills
Other ways to install

  • From a shell:

    claude plugin install rest --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills

  • In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box, then Plugins, Add marketplace with LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills, then Add plugin.

Read bounding-autonomous-work Source on GitHub

Commands

CommandWhat it does
/restrest every session with this mod for 8 hours
/rest 45mthe same for 45 minutes; 2h, 90m work too (1 minute to 24 hours)
/rest here 2hrest this session alone
/rest offend the rest for every session, and this session's own
/rest statuswho rests, since when, until when, and what this session holds

In use

/rest while a rest is in force says so and changes nothing; /rest <length> starts a new one. A prompt you type in a resting session wakes that session alone, and the others keep resting.

The mod registers no tool for the model, and /rest changes nothing unless you typed it. A session never pauses your other sessions, or wakes itself, on its own.

How it behaves

  • Holding. Each session checks the rest before every tool call, its subagents' included, and waits there while it rests, re-reading the rest every two seconds with the host's sleep. A prompt that is not yours (a plugin's, a schedule's, a task's notification, another session's, a channel's) waits the same way, so nothing starts a turn during a rest. Interrupting still works: the held call stops waiting and never runs.
  • Ending. A rest ends by itself at its end time: 8 hours unless you gave a length, 24 hours at most, so a forgotten rest cannot freeze sessions you open tomorrow. /rest off ends it at once.
  • Showing. A resting session's status line reads resting until 18:30, with , 2 held while calls wait. A session learns of a rest started elsewhere within five seconds, and says so once with a toast, and again when it wakes.
  • Not yet confirmed live. Sessions learn of a rest by reading the mod's own store file. That every running session re-reads that file has not been checked with two live sessions. After starting a rest, /rest status in a second session shows whether it saw it.
  • What it cannot stop. A model response that is already streaming finishes; the session stops at its next tool call. A turn that calls no tool simply ends. Shell commands already running in the background keep running. Sessions without the mod, and other machines, are not affected.
  • Waking costs. After a long rest the prompt cache has usually expired, so the first request after waking reads the whole conversation again at full price.
  • Where it cannot hold. Where sleep is not on the PATH (or not a CLI session), the mod cannot hold a call: /rest says so and starts nothing, and that session never waits. Other harnesses ignore this mod.
